title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ecclesiastes chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ecclesiastes Chapter 6.

questions.question: What is the evil that the author has seen under the sun and says is common among men?
options: A man given riches but unable to enjoy them
A man who is poor and miserable
A man who lives a short life
A man who is wise but not honored
questions.correctAnswer: A man given riches but unable to enjoy them
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:1 describes an evil common among men, which is further explained in verse 2 as a man blessed with riches but unable to enjoy them.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 6, what does God give to a man besides riches and honour?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:2 states that although God gives riches, wealth, and honour, He does not give the man power to eat thereof, meaning to enjoy his possessions.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 6:3, what is said to be better than a man who begets a hundred children and lives many years but his soul is not filled with good?
options: A wealthy man with few children
A wise man with no children
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:3 states that an untimely birth is better than a man who has many children and years but whose soul is not filled with good and who has no burial.

questions.question: What happens to the name of the man who comes in with vanity and departs in darkness?
options: It shall be covered with darkness
It is recorded in the book of life
It is remembered by his children
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be covered with darkness
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:4 explains that the name of such a man shall be covered with darkness.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 6:5, who has more rest than the man who lives many years without good?
options: He who has not seen the sun nor known any thing
He who is wise and poor
questions.correctAnswer: He who has not seen the sun nor known any thing
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:5 states that the man who has not seen the sun nor known any thing has more rest than the other.

questions.question: True or False: According to Ecclesiastes 6:6, even if a man lives a thousand years twice told, he has seen no good.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:6 clearly states that even living a thousand years twice told, the man has seen no good.

questions.question: What is all the labour of man for, according to Ecclesiastes 6:7?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:7 states that all the labour of man is for his mouth, meaning to satisfy his hunger or needs.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 6:8 asks what the poor has that knows to walk before the living.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:8 contains the question, 'what hath the poor, that knoweth to walk before the living?' affirming the statement as true.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 6:9, what is better than the wandering of the desire?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:9 says, 'Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire.'

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 6:10, who is named already and cannot contend with the mightier?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:10 states that 'that which hath been is named already, and it is known that it is man' who cannot contend with the mightier.

questions.question: What question does Ecclesiastes 6:11 raise about the increase of vanity?
options: What is man the better for?
questions.correctAnswer: What is man the better for?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:11 asks, 'Seeing there be many things that increase vanity, what is man the better?'

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 6:12 states that man knows what is good for him in this life.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:12 says, 'For who knoweth what is good for man in this life?' indicating that man does not know what is good for him.

questions.question: In Ecclesiastes 6, what is described as an 'evil disease'?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:2 describes a man given riches but not power to enjoy them, calling it 'vanity, and it is an evil disease.'

questions.question: True or False: According to Ecclesiastes 6:7, the appetite of man is always filled by his labour.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:7 says 'yet the appetite is not filled,' meaning labour does not always satisfy man's desires.

questions.question: In Ecclesiastes 6, which event is described first?
options: A man given riches but unable to enjoy them
A man who begets a hundred children and lives many years without good
An untimely birth being better than a long life without good
A man departing in darkness with his name covered
questions.correctAnswer: A man given riches but unable to enjoy them
questions.explanation: The first event described in the chapter is in verse 1 and 2 about a man who has riches but cannot enjoy them.

medium.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ecclesiastes Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 6:5, who has more rest: the man who has many years but no satisfaction, or the man who has not seen the sun nor known anything?
options: The man with many years but no satisfaction
The man who has not seen the sun nor known anything
questions.correctAnswer: The man who has not seen the sun nor known anything
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:5 states that the man who has not seen the sun nor known anything has more rest than the other who lives many years without satisfaction. This highlights the vanity of a long life without fulfillment.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 6:6 teach about the value of a very long life without seeing good?
options: It is a blessing to live a thousand years
Even a thousand years twice told is meaningless without good
The wise will always see good in a long life
questions.correctAnswer: Even a thousand years twice told is meaningless without good
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:6 emphasizes that living a very long life, even twice a thousand years, is meaningless if one sees no good. This shows that the quality of life matters more than length.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 6:7 describe the labor of man in relation to appetite?
options: Man labors for wealth, which fills the appetite
Man labors for his mouth, yet the appetite is never fully satisfied
Appetite is always fulfilled by labor
questions.correctAnswer: Man labors for his mouth, yet the appetite is never fully satisfied
questions.explanation: According to Ecclesiastes 6:7, all the labor of man is for his mouth, but the appetite is not filled, indicating human desire and satisfaction are often unfulfilled despite hard work.

questions.question: From Ecclesiastes 6:8, what is the difference between the wise and the fool, or the poor who walk before the living?
options: The wise have more wealth than the fool
The poor are less righteous than the wise
The wise have no more than the fool, and the poor know how to walk before the living
The fool has more wisdom than the wise
questions.correctAnswer: The wise have no more than the fool, and the poor know how to walk before the living
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:8 questions the advantage of wisdom over foolishness and notes that the poor know how to live before the living, highlighting equality in human condition and behavior.

questions.question: What practical lesson about contentment can we learn from Ecclesiastes 6:7, which says all labor is for the mouth but the appetite is not filled?
options: To continually strive for more wealth
To find satisfaction only in material things
To understand that earthly labor alone cannot satisfy the soul
questions.correctAnswer: To understand that earthly labor alone cannot satisfy the soul
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:7 teaches that despite all labor to satisfy physical needs, appetite remains unfilled, implying that true satisfaction comes beyond mere earthly toil, encouraging trust in God for contentment.

questions.question: Based on Ecclesiastes 6:5-6, how does the passage challenge the value of a long life without meaningful experience?
options: It encourages accumulating wealth for a long life
It suggests that a long life without seeing good is vanity and offers less rest
It says only the length of life matters
It promises eternal life to those living long
questions.correctAnswer: It suggests that a long life without seeing good is vanity and offers less rest
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 6 together show that even a long life without fulfillment or good is vanity and less restful than a brief life without such experiences, emphasizing quality over quantity of life.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 6:8 prompt believers to reflect on wisdom and humility?
options: It shows the wise are always superior to fools
It reveals that wisdom doesn't guarantee more than foolishness, prompting humility
It instructs to seek riches above wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals that wisdom doesn't guarantee more than foolishness, prompting humility
questions.explanation: Verse 8 points out the lack of significant advantage of the wise over the fool, encouraging humility and trust in God rather than pride in human wisdom.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 6:9 states that the wandering of desire is better than the sight of the eyes.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:9 actually says that the sight of the eyes is better than the wandering of the desire, highlighting the vanity and vexation of spirit caused by unfulfilled desires.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 6:10 teach about man's ability to contend with greater powers?
options: Man can always overcome mightier powers
Man may not contend with him that is mightier
Man should seek to fight greater powers
questions.correctAnswer: Man may not contend with him that is mightier
questions.explanation: Verse 10 explains that man is limited and cannot contend with mightier beings, teaching humility and recognizing human limitations before God's sovereignty.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 6:11, what is the effect of many things increasing vanity?
options: Man is unchanged or no better despite vanity increasing
questions.correctAnswer: Man is unchanged or no better despite vanity increasing
questions.explanation: Verse 11 questions what benefit man gains from the increase of vanity, suggesting that despite many things increasing vanity, man is not better off, calling for trust in God rather than worldly pursuits.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 6:12 reminds us that no one truly knows what is good for man during the days of his life.
questions.explanation: Verse 12 states that no one knows what is good for man during his vain life, highlighting human uncertainty and the need for reliance on God’s wisdom.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 6:4 describe the fate of a man who lives many years without satisfaction or a proper burial?
options: He departs in brightness and honor
He comes in vanity and departs in darkness, his name covered with darkness
questions.correctAnswer: He comes in vanity and departs in darkness, his name covered with darkness
questions.explanation: Verse 4 says such a man comes in vanity and departs in darkness, with his name covered by darkness, illustrating the futility and obscurity of a life without fulfillment.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 6:3 say about the value of an untimely birth compared to a long life without satisfaction?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 states that an untimely birth is better than a man who lives many years without his soul being filled with good and without a proper burial, emphasizing the vanity of a long but unsatisfactory life.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 6:2 describes a man who has riches but does not have the power to enjoy them, and this situation is called an evil disease.
questions.explanation: Verse 2 describes a man to whom God has given wealth and honor, but who lacks the power to enjoy it, with a stranger eating it, and calls this vanity and an evil disease.

questions.question: Based on Ecclesiastes 6:7-8, how should believers view their labor and wisdom in the context of life's vanity?
options: Labor is endless and appetite unfilled; wisdom is not superior to foolishness, prompting humility and trust in God
The wise have advantage over others in all things
questions.correctAnswer: Labor is endless and appetite unfilled; wisdom is not superior to foolishness, prompting humility and trust in God
questions.explanation: Verses 7 and 8 together teach that despite labor, appetite is unfilled and wisdom does not guarantee superiority over fools, encouraging humility and reliance on God rather than human effort alone.

hard.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ecclesiastes Chapter 6.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 6:9, what is considered better than the wandering of desire?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:9 explicitly states, 'Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire,' emphasizing the value of actual experience over unfulfilled longing.

questions.question: In Ecclesiastes 6:10, what cannot man contend with?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:10 teaches that man cannot contend with 'him that is mightier than he,' highlighting human limitation against divine power.

questions.question: What question does the author pose in Ecclesiastes 6:11 regarding vanity?
options: Seeing there be many things that increase vanity, what is man the better?
Why do the righteous suffer in vanity?
How can vanity be overcome by wisdom?
Is vanity more powerful than death?
questions.correctAnswer: Seeing there be many things that increase vanity, what is man the better?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:11 questions the benefit to man despite the increase in vanity, reflecting the theme of life's futility.

questions.question: Ecclesiastes 6:12 compares man's life to what?
questions.explanation: The verse describes man's life as 'a shadow,' signifying brevity and insubstantiality.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of life's vanity and brevity similar to Ecclesiastes 6:12?
questions.explanation: Psalm 39:6 similarly reflects on the fleeting nature of life as a 'shadow,' connecting with Ecclesiastes 6:12's theme of life's transience.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Ecclesiastes 6:10 where it states 'That which hath been is named already'?
questions.explanation: The phrase forms an inclusio framing the inevitability and repetitiveness of human existence, a common literary device in wisdom literature.

questions.question: In Ecclesiastes 6:8, what two groups are compared?
questions.explanation: The verse contrasts the wise and the fool, questioning what advantage the wise have over the fool.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 6:7, what is the labor of man for?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'All the labour of man is for his mouth,' meaning all human effort is to satisfy hunger and needs.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 6:5 states that a man who has not seen the sun nor known anything has more rest than one who lives many years filled with no good.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:5 explicitly says the man who has not seen the sun nor known anything 'hath more rest than the other,' affirming the answer.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 6:2 praises a man to whom God has given riches, wealth, and honour, stating he will always enjoy his desires.
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:2 states that even if a man has riches and honour but does not enjoy them himself, it is vanity and an evil disease, negating the praise.

questions.question: Which Hebrew word concept is central to Ecclesiastes 6:9's use of 'vanity' and 'vexation of spirit'?
questions.explanation: 'Hevel' is the Hebrew word translated as 'vanity' or 'vapor,' emphasizing life’s fleeting and elusive nature as presented in Ecclesiastes 6:9.

questions.question: Ecclesiastes 6:1 mentions 'an evil which I have seen under the sun.' What is this evil described as?
questions.explanation: The verse states the evil is 'common among men,' indicating it is widespread and frequently observed.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 6:4 describe the departure of a man who lives many years without good?
questions.explanation: The verse says the man 'departeth in darkness,' symbolizing obscurity and lack of remembrance.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of human limitation against divine power found in Ecclesiastes 6:10?
questions.explanation: Romans 9:20 discusses the limitation of human beings in contending with God’s will, echoing Ecclesiastes 6:10's theme.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 6:3 suggest is better than living a long life without good or a proper burial?
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'an untimely birth is better' than a long life without fulfillment or burial.

theological.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ecclesiastes Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 6:1 reveal about the nature of certain evils seen under the sun?
options: They are only seen by the wise
They are only found among the rich
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:1 states that there is an evil which is common among men, indicating a widespread human condition.

questions.question: In Ecclesiastes 6:2, what is described as vanity in relation to a man who has wealth?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:2 describes a man who has been given riches but lacks the power to eat from them, highlighting the vanity of wealth without enjoyment.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 6:3 suggest about a man who begets many children but lives without fulfillment?
options: His life is full of joy
He is better than an untimely birth
An untimely birth is better than he
questions.correctAnswer: An untimely birth is better than he
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:3 states that if a man lives many years without fulfillment, it is better for an untimely birth, indicating the value of fulfillment over mere existence.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'cometh in with vanity' in Ecclesiastes 6:4 imply about human existence?
options: Life begins and ends in futility
Life is meant to be enjoyed
questions.correctAnswer: Life begins and ends in futility
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:4 suggests that life is characterized by vanity and ends in darkness, emphasizing the transient nature of human existence.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 6:5, what is said about those who have not seen the sun?
options: They are better off than the living
They will be judged more harshly
They have more knowledge than the living
questions.correctAnswer: They are better off than the living
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:5 states that those who have not seen the sun have more rest than the living, suggesting that a life without suffering or experience can be seen as a blessing.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 6:6 reveal about the value of a long life without goodness?
options: It is preferable to have a short life full of joy
It is better than living a short life
questions.correctAnswer: It is preferable to have a short life full of joy
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:6 indicates that even living a thousand years without experiencing good is ultimately meaningless, highlighting the importance of quality over quantity in life.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 6:8 suggest about the difference between the wise and the fool?
options: What hath the wise more than the fool?
questions.correctAnswer: What hath the wise more than the fool?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:8 questions the advantage of the wise over the fool, pointing to the futility of wisdom without meaningful outcomes.

questions.question: In Ecclesiastes 6:9, what is considered better than the wandering of desire?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:9 states that better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire, emphasizing contentment with what one has over unfulfilled longing.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 6:10 imply about humanity's position before God?
options: Humans are aware of their destiny
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:10 emphasizes that man cannot contend with the one who is mightier, highlighting human limitations and the sovereignty of God.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 6:11, what increases vanity?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:11 points out that many things increase vanity, indicating that human pursuits often lead to emptiness.

questions.question: What is the central theme of Ecclesiastes 6:12 regarding human life?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:12 describes life as a shadow, emphasizing its fleeting nature and the uncertainty of what follows, posing existential questions about human existence.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Ecclesiastes 6:2 and 6:9 convey about wealth and desire?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:2 shows the futility of wealth without enjoyment, while 6:9 emphasizes the superiority of contentment over unfulfilled desire, highlighting the emptiness of chasing after wealth.

questions.question: How do Ecclesiastes 6:5 and 6:12 connect to the understanding of life’s brevity?
options: Life is a gift from God
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:5 suggests that those who have not lived are better off, and 6:12 emphasizes the ephemeral nature of life, conveying that human existence is temporary and uncertain.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 6:10 and 6:11 reveal about the nature of humanity in relation to God?
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:10 reveals that man cannot contend with the might of God, and 6:11 suggests that human pursuits often result in vanity, highlighting humanity's insignificance before God.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that wealth guarantees happiness. What does Ecclesiastes 6:2 teach about wealth?
options: Wealth is the key to a fulfilled life
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 6:2 indicates that having riches without the ability to enjoy them renders wealth meaningless, countering the sceptic's claim about wealth guaranteeing happiness.
